figures.name: stt_engine_accuracy
figures.caption: Word error rate and number handling for both recognizers on the committed audio benchmark. The raw word error rate is shown in grey to expose how much of it is spelling: Canary wrote numbers as words, Whisper writes numerals, and only the number-normalised bars compare the engines. The right panel separates transcribing a long number correctly from keeping it out of the released text - the two are not the same thing, and the engines differ in opposite directions.

figures.name: stt_engine_cost
figures.caption: Real-time factor and end-to-end latency for both recognizers. The dashed line is real time: a bar below it means the device processes speech faster than it arrives. Bars are drawn only for arms that have been measured.

figures.name: stt_engine_released_identifiers
figures.caption: The end-to-end privacy question that survives a change of recognizer: after masking and after the display renderer, is an identifier-scale number still legible in what the device released? It needs no alignment against the reference and no gold offsets, which is what makes it comparable across engines where the entity-level metrics are not.
